figures.finding: No collective contract or statutory minimum sets a screen actor's pay in New Zealand: the Employment Relations Authority shows no occupational contract in force for performers, and the SPADA/Equity individual performance agreement leaves every fee line blank for negotiation.

value.framework: Screen Industry Workers Act 2022 (in force 30 December 2022) allows a performers' occupational contract; none in force
value.standard_form: SPADA / NZ Actors' Equity Individual Performance Agreement (2013): fees filled in per engagement; minimum call 5 hours

sources.said: All information for the application to initiate bargaining for an occupational contract applying to performers is available on this page. There is currently no occupational contract in force.

As agreed between The Screen Production and Development Association and New Zealand Actors’ Equity for use on New Zealand based productions … Minimum call 5 hours for Performance or Rehearsal Call … Fee and other payments (some of these may not apply to the Artist) Performance Weekly Rate (if applicable) $ Performance Daily Rate $ Performance Hourly Rate $ Non-Performance Daily Rate $ Half Day Rate 60% of applicable daily rate

This collective bargaining will result in a baseline contract called an “Occupational Contract” that will set the terms of engagement , working conditions and minimum pay rates for designated Occupational Groups (performers are one of these groups).
Our unwavering expectation is that SPADA will promptly honour their 2021 commitment to SIWA registration so that our sector can move forward with certainty.

figures.finding: On stage, Equity New Zealand has collective agreements with The Court Theatre in Christchurch (26 April 2024 to 25 April 2026) and Auckland Theatre Company (1 January to 31 December 2024).

agreements.name: Equity New Zealand / The Court Theatre Collective Agreement

figures.applies: New Zealand, actors employed directly by these two theatres on fixed terms.

sources.said: 1.1 The Court Theatre Trust (the “Employer”); and 1.2 Equity New Zealand Incorporated (the “Union”) … 18.1 The Term of this Agreement is for 24 months, coming into force on 26 April 2024 and shall continue in force until its expiry on 25 April 2026.
45.1 This Agreement shall be effective from 1 January 2024 until 31 December 2024.

In recent years we have been able to work alongside both Auckland Theatre Company and The Court Theatre to create mutually beneficial Collective Agreements, that set minimums and expectations for all parties.

figures.finding: The Court Theatre's minimum for a lead was $1,292 a week ($1,800 with six years' experience) from 26 April 2024, and $1,327.53 ($1,849.50) after the 2.75% rise of 26 April 2025; supporting roles were $1,200 ($1,600), then $1,233 ($1,644).

value.pair: [minimum, minimum with at least six years' relevant experience]
value.hours: salary covers all hours; time and a half beyond 50 hours in production week (salaried) or 10 hours a day (waged); 12-hour break (10 by agreement); one day off a week

figures.finding: Auckland is the main market: firms in the Auckland region earned 58% of screen-sector revenue (NZ$1.8 billion) in the year to March 2021, Wellington 37% (NZ$1.2 billion), Wellington leading in post-production.

value.older: Auckland >75% of screen industry revenue, 2008/09 (Stats NZ via WIFT NZ)

figures.applies: New Zealand, whole screen sector, tax year ending March 2021 (MBIE, February 2024).

sources.said: The Auckland region generated a total revenue of $1.8 billion in 2021, 58% of the sector’s total. This was followed by the Wellington region with 37% of the total revenue at $1.2 billion

Statistics New Zealand's Screen Industry Survey Regional Data for 2008/09 , released last week, shows the Auckland region dominated the New Zealand screen industry last year in both total revenue and number of businesses, while the Wellington region was ahead in feature film and post-production revenue. Although Auckland's revenue dropped by 6 percent in 2009, to $2.2 billion, it still made up more than three-quarters of the total screen industry takings nationwide.
